<thought>We need the number of chemically equivalent hydrogen atoms (unique proton environments) in the compound. The only way to get that information is to obtain the 1H NMR spectrum, which the `proton_nmr_spectra` tool can provide without any arguments. The spectrum will list the distinct signals, and the count of those signals equals the number of unique hydrogen environments. We'll call the tool and then count the signals from its output.</thought>
<action>proton_nmr_spectra</action>
<action_input>{}</action_input>
